foreignRepresentativeOffice_description_: During market expansion in Vietnam, many foreign traders choose to establish a Representative Office (RO) as a strategic step to understand the market, promote trade, and build partnerships before making deeper investments.
This model is suitable for businesses that want a legal presence in Vietnam but do not yet directly conduct profit-generating business activities.

foreignRepresentativeOffice_section1_tit: What is a representative office of a foreign company?
foreignRepresentativeOffice_section1_int: A representative office is a dependent unit of a foreign trader permitted to operate in Vietnam with the following functions:
foreignRepresentativeOffice_section1_ite: Monitoring the implementation of contracts of the parent company
foreignRepresentativeOffice_section1_not: Note: A representative office is not allowed to directly conduct profit-generating business activities in Vietnam and cannot issue invoices.
foreignRepresentativeOffice_section2_tit: Conditions for establishing a representative office of a foreign company
foreignRepresentativeOffice_section2_int: Foreign traders are permitted to establish representative offices in Vietnam when meeting the following conditions:
foreignRepresentativeOffice_section2_ite: The trader must be legally established and registered in a country or territory that participates in an international treaty to which Vietnam is a member, or is recognized by the laws of such country or territory.
The trader must have been operating for at least one year since its establishment or registration.
If the business registration certificate specifies a duration of operation, it must remain valid for at least one year from the date of application submission.
The activities of the Representative Office must be consistent with Vietnam's international commitments.
foreignRepresentativeOffice_section2_not: Note: If the activities are inconsistent with international commitments or the trader is from a country or territory without a treaty with Vietnam, establishment must be approved by the Minister or the competent specialized authority.

extension_capital_contribution_project_p: Extension of the capital contribution deadline - Project implementation progress
Investment & Enterprise

During the implementation of investment projects, there are circumstances where investors are unable to fully contribute capital or complete project components in accordance with the registered schedule due to market fluctuations, financial constraints, delays in land handover, or other objective factors.

In such cases, businesses need to carry out procedures to extend the capital contribution and/or project implementation schedule to ensure compliance with legal regulations and avoid the risk of penalties.
This extension amends the content of the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC), and therefore requires approval from the competent authority before further implementation.
1. Cases requiring an extension

According to the provisions of the 2020 Enterprise Law, from the date of issuance of the Business Registration Certificate and the Investment Registration Certificate, investors are obligated to fully contribute the registered capital within 90 days or in accordance with the schedule specified in the IRC.

If, as the committed deadline approaches, the investor has not yet completed or fully contributed the registered capital, the enterprise must carry out the procedure to adjust and extend the capital contribution schedule before the deadline expires.

Proactively carrying out the extension procedure at the right time not only helps the enterprise comply with legal regulations and avoid the risk of administrative penalties, but also ensures that investment activities are maintained continuously, stably, and legally.
2. Scope of services provided by PGU

When clients choose the service of extending the capital contribution schedule, PGU will act on behalf of the business to implement all necessary tasks to ensure that the procedures are carried out correctly and on time.
2.1. In-depth legal consulting

PGU reviews project documents, assesses the actual capital contribution status, and provides detailed advice on regulations related to amending the Investment Registration Certificate, especially regarding the extension of the capital contribution deadline.
Simultaneously, it proposes appropriate solutions to minimize legal risks for investors.
2.2. Drafting and implementing the adjustment procedure

Preparing all necessary documents; acting as an authorized representative to submit the application, monitoring the processing, and receiving the results of the adjustment to extend the capital contribution schedule at the Industrial Park Management Board, Economic Zone Management Board, or the Department of Finance where the enterprise is implementing the project.
2.3. Representative working with the inspection agency (if any)

In cases where the extension is granted after the committed capital contribution deadline has passed, PGU will assist in preparing the explanatory documents and directly participate in working with the Inspectorate of the Department of Finance to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the enterprise.
2.4. Support in fulfilling investment reporting obligations

Reviewing the status of project reporting; assisting in preparing and submitting supplementary reports as required by investment management agencies, ensuring that businesses fully comply with legal regulations.
3. Reasons why investors should choose PGU

Investment expertise: PGU's team of lawyers has experience advising on legal regulations related to capital contribution schedules and project implementation timelines, helping investors to renew their projects in accordance with the law.

Project status assessment and consultation on suitable options: PGU assists in reviewing the project implementation status, capital contribution progress, and related legal conditions to advise on extension options that comply with the regulations of the investment management agency.

Prepare documents and expedite procedures: We assist in drafting documents, explaining the reasons for extension, and working with the investment registration authority to efficiently carry out the project schedule adjustment procedures.

Minimizing legal risks for investors: Failure to comply with regulations regarding project extensions can lead to penalties or project termination. PGU assists investors in following the correct procedures, minimizing legal risks.

Legal support throughout the project implementation process: PGU is ready to support investors with legal issues arising during the project implementation in Vietnam, from project adjustments to ongoing legal advice.

With practical experience in investment and business, PGU is committed to accompanying investors, providing timely, comprehensive, and effective legal solutions throughout the project renewal and implementation process.

cases_requiring_registration_intro: Pursuant to Article 11 of Circular No. 12/2022/TT-NHNN, foreign loans must be registered with the State Bank of Vietnam in the following cases:
case_medium_long_term_loans_title: 1.1. Medium and long-term loans from foreign lenders
case_medium_long_term_loans_desc: All loans with medium-term or long-term durations are subject to mandatory registration.
case_short_term_extended_title: 1.2. Short-term loans extended beyond the original maturity
case_short_term_extended_desc: If a loan initially classified as short-term is extended and the total loan duration exceeds one year, the loan must be registered.
case_short_term_outstanding_after_one_ye: 1.3. Short-term loans with outstanding principal after one year

For short-term loans without extension agreements, if at the time one year has passed from the first disbursement there remains outstanding principal (including capitalized interest), the enterprise must register the loan with the State Bank.
case_no_registration_desc: If the borrower fully repays the outstanding principal within 30 working days from the one-year threshold mentioned above, registration is not required.
case_summary_desc: All medium-term and long-term foreign loans must be registered. foreign_loan_cases_requiring_registratio: 1. Cases Requiring Registration of Changes to Foreign Loans
cases_requiring_registration_description: Where there are adjustments relating to a foreign loan already confirmed by the State Bank of Vietnam, enterprises must determine whether such changes fall under mere notification through the electronic system or require formal registration of loan amendments.
Proper classification helps avoid violations of foreign exchange management regulations and ensures smooth disbursement and repayment processes.
cases_only_notification_title: Cases where only notification on the electronic system is required (no registration required)
cases_only_notification_item_1: Adjusting the time for capital withdrawal or principal repayment within a maximum of 10 working days compared to the plan confirmed by the State Bank of Vietnam.
cases_only_notification_item_2: Changing the registered office address without changing the province or city where the head office is located; the enterprise must notify the authority that confirmed the loan.
cases_only_notification_item_3: Changes to lenders or related information in syndicated loans that designate representatives of the lenders, except where such changes alter the representative role of the lender.
cases_only_notification_item_4: Changing the trade name of the bank providing account services or the bank servicing the secured transaction.
cases_only_notification_item_5: Adjusting the interest and fee payment plan compared to the confirmed plan without changing the method of determining interest and fees as agreed in the loan agreement; the enterprise must prepare an interest and fee calculation sheet for the bank to verify when transferring funds.
cases_only_notification_item_6: Adjusting the amount of capital withdrawal, principal repayment, interest, and fees by increasing or decreasing it within 100 units of the loan currency compared to the previously confirmed content.
cases_only_notification_item_7: The actual disbursement or principal repayment in a given period is lower than the registered plan.
cases_requiring_registration_change_desc: Except for the cases that only require notification through the electronic system, any changes relating to the loan contents recorded in the loan registration confirmation or loan change registration confirmation issued by the State Bank of Vietnam must be formally registered in accordance with applicable regulations.

capital_transfer_section_what_is_desc_1: Capital transfer refers to the transfer of ownership of all or part of shares or capital contributions from one individual or organization to another.
capital_transfer_condition_single_member: The owner has the full right to transfer part or all of their capital contribution to another individual or organization.
capital_transfer_condition_multi_member_: 2.2. For limited liability companies with two or more members

- According to Article 52 of the 2020 Enterprise Law, as amended and supplemented in 2025, a member intending to transfer their capital contribution must offer that contribution to the remaining members in proportion to the remaining members' capital contributions in the company, under the same offering conditions.

- Only if the remaining members do not purchase or do not purchase all of the shares within 30 days of the offer date will that member be entitled to transfer the shares to a non-member under conditions no more favorable than those offered to the remaining members.
capital_transfer_condition_joint_stock_d: - According to Article 127 of the 2020 Enterprise Law, shares are freely transferable, except for common shares of founding shareholders and when the company's charter stipulates restrictions on share transfer.

- Within three years from the date the company is granted its Certificate of Business Registration, the common shares of founding shareholders may be freely transferred to other founding shareholders, and may only be transferred to non-founding shareholders with the approval of the General Meeting of Shareholders.
